# The defect-yield list (spec 2026-10-29-chart-parser-design.md, sections 2.3 and 8).
# Fixed 2026-10-29 from `git zhi list --format json` (every open issue on the chain).
# 182 open issues; 152 bodies read (the 30 chart-waypoint and
# m2-incremental issues are planned work, not defects, and were excluded by title).
# Rule: an issue is listed when its body records a Perl source on which
# internal/parse or internal/lexer reaches a different verdict than perl's:
# it refuses what perl compiles, accepts what perl refuses, or builds a tree
# perl does not. Disagreements only in typing, lowering, canon re-emission,
# line numbering or .tpm declarations are not listed.
# 50 listed; 44 have a frozen case in defect-yield/<ref>.pl.
# 01a174d8-40e3 and 01a17591-1a24 share one title and one defect family, so that
# family counts twice in the yield; both stay listed because their cases differ.
# Already settled by recursive descent at 0e8c32fd (the cases no longer disagree):
# 01a0d0b1-2343 01a0dccb-5c5f 01a122e2-3982 01a11263-4044 01a11254-136b
# 01a12204-5275 01a128ad-18f3 01a13216-6a20 01a16b2b-44dd 01a11106-b336 01a16a7a-a71c
# The list is fixed: settling an issue changes its state, not this file.
01a0d0b1-2343 The block form of the filehandle slot refuses
01a0dc72-2609 Bare v5 is a v-string in perl, and a lexer cannot tell it from a bareword
01a0dccb-5c5f A malformed format declaration loses canon's fixpoint, and one perl rejects parses clean
01a10e49-133f Refuse map/grep forms perl rejects: hash brace then a term-position operator, block at EOF
01a110de-6b63 sub g : method lvalue {} is refused; perl accepts space-separated attributes after one colon
01a110e9-e23e Two declaration comma shapes still disagree with perl: list declarations, and a later low-precedence operator

01a11106-b1e8 Read IO::File's computed export list, so T1's indirect_object_constructor.t returns to 0
01a11106-b336 A lexical sub is also recorded in its package and outlives its block
01a11254-136b Four trees that disagree with perl, found building the arity refusal: pipe my(...) or die, indirect new/is, f { } for (&@), canon (&$)
01a11263-4044 The arity refusal misses XS subs whose prototypes are not in readable source (blessed, first)
01a112f8-4f6c CORE::any { } @a without its feature is left unparsed; perl accepts it
01a11317-84f4 A niladic builtin called with arguments is not refused: time(1) parses as time()(1)
01a1201b-1f6e say is read as the builtin whether or not the say feature is on
01a1201c-36fa An undeclared bareword argument is read as a sub call where perl reads a string
01a121e3-0f49 state is always a declarator in internal/parse, but perl reads it as a bareword when its feature is off
01a12204-5275 The lexer cannot know a bareword is a declared sub, so & and * after one are read as perl reads them only when it is
01a12204-533c A heredoc with no terminator parses, though perl cannot find the string terminator
01a122e2-3982 use 'A', use $x, use;, use {A} and use 5.010 (1) parse, though perl refuses each
01a12312-774d my $0 parses, though perl cannot use a global in my
01a123c3-5915 Three neighbours of print's handle rule: - A is a string, a bareword handle before -1/&y, and the rule after any list operator
01a1244d-a4b2 while(){} is refused by internal/parse, though perl reads the empty condition as while (1)
01a12573-eb8a Canon is not a fixpoint on *+ ++ (a fuzz find)
01a128ad-18f3 &2 and &== 2 are accepted by perl, which names the sub by one character; internal/parse refuses or misreads them
01a12a7a-db26 A sub declared in another package is refused as a call from main, where perl reads an indirect method call
01a12a7a-dbdf Unfeatured fc $x is refused, where perl reads the indirect call $x->fc

01a1335d-9738 A chained comparison draws a false operand warning, as legacy read it pairwise
01a13e28-6ad8 The parser ignores use lib, so imports from a use lib directory go unresolved
01a142d2-5f8d A compound operator after declaration attributes is accepted, though perl refuses it
01a142d2-602e print STDOUT **2 produces a tree, though perl refuses it
01a1447f-7f64 A fully-qualified call with a parenless argument list is refused: Carp::croak sprintf(...)
01a1447f-80d7 print FH &{...}(...) is refused
01a1448a-e64a package Foo v1.2.3 { } is refused, though perl accepts a v-string version
01a146bc-6132 A scalar typed our outside a .tpm is not refused, though perl dies No such class

01a16a7a-a71c \my swallows the assignment that follows it
01a16ab2-e045 A builtin overridden by an import still parses as the builtin
01a16b2b-44dd A bareword operator word as a hash subscript key parses as the operator
